current_episode.title: This CEO Says Quarterly Thinking Is “Insane.” His Company Is Building a Hotel Designed to Stand for 100 Years

guest.bio_context: Alistair Darby joined Sir Richard Sutton Limited in December 2023 as CEO with a background as a hospitality operator across multiple CEO roles, primarily in public companies. He was brought on board to drive the operational agenda and transform the company from a longstanding asset manager of properties, farms, and hotels into an active hospitality operator. He is leading the company's transition to directly manage three regional hotels (Bath, Windsor, and the Athenaeum in London) and overseeing major refurbishment and development projects, including a significant new hotel build in Mayfair planned to stand for 100 years.

pending_qa.q: What role does curiosity play in effective CEO leadership?
pending_qa.r: Darby emphasizes that his longstanding mentor valued natural curiosity above all else when recruiting—the ability to look at a situation, narrow your eyes, and ask if that is really the case. Curiosity drives better decision-making because it leads to genuine inquiry beyond surface-level answers and uncovers what guests truly want. Without curiosity, leaders make assumptions that prove incorrect.

pending_qa.q: How does active listening enhance leadership effectiveness in hospitality?
pending_qa.r: Darby credits his wife Alex, an executive coach, as a master of active listening who reads what lies behind what is said. He emphasizes that listening is everything in hospitality and is a direct follow-on from curiosity—if you are genuinely curious, you must listen and listen beyond the first and second answers. Good listening requires patience and genuine interest in understanding what others are really communicating.
